_origin: Adapted from a public postmortem; names, times and numbers changed.

incident.title: EdgeProxy5xxFlapping
incident.description: edge-proxy: 5xx rate swinging between 1% and 45% every few minutes on all points of presence since 11:21 UTC (threshold 1%).

initial_context: Shown before any check. At 11:31 UTC our public status page, hosted by a third-party provider and not behind our edge, also stopped loading. Last month a peer was hit by a pulsed HTTP flood that switched on and off every few minutes, and the on-call channel suspects the same. Changes in the last 24 hours: 11:05 analytics-db permissions cleanup, rolling node by node; 10:40 bot-score service v8.4 to all regions; 10:00-12:00 DNS provider scheduled maintenance; 09:15 edge-proxy v57.0 to 50% of nodes (the other half run v56.3).

hypotheses.attack: An attack is overloading the edge and our status page.
hypotheses.config_file: Configuration or data pushed to the edge nodes is making them fail.
hypotheses.proxy_release: The edge-proxy v57.0 release introduced a bug.
hypotheses.bot_score_release: The bot-score service v8.4 deploy returns bad responses that fail requests.
hypotheses.kv_store: The edge key-value store is failing, and requests that read from it error.
hypotheses.dns: The DNS provider maintenance is breaking name resolution for the edge.

traffic_by_source.description: Edge request rate by source network, and requests flagged by flood detection.
traffic_by_source.result: 11:00-11:40 UTC. Offered requests per second 38-40M, the same as this hour last week. Top 10 source networks: 2.8% of requests, normal. Flagged by flood detection: 0.01%. The 5xx swings do not follow traffic: 5xx rose to 45% at 11:26 and 11:36 while traffic stayed flat.

status_page_provider.description: Status of the third-party provider hosting the public status page.
status_page_provider.result: The provider's own status page reports 'Elevated errors on hosted status pages' from 11:29 to 11:52 UTC, across all its customers. Our status page receives no traffic through our edge.

errors_by_version.result: v56.3 (50% of nodes) and v57.0 (50% of nodes) swing together: 11:26 44% and 46%; 11:31 2% and 1%; 11:36 45% and 44%. Before 11:20 both under 0.2%.

proxy_panics.description: edge-proxy crash and panic messages, 11:00-11:40 UTC.
proxy_panics.result: 182,000 lines 'panic in bot module: feature table has 212 entries, limit 200 (preallocated)', from both versions, first at 11:20:48. Each follows 'loaded bot feature file' within 50ms. Between the bursts, nodes log 'loaded bot feature file (58 entries)' and serve normally.

feature_file_history.description: The last 12 versions of the bot feature file, generated every 5 minutes from analytics-db and pushed to all edge nodes.
feature_file_history.result: Up to 11:15: 57-58 entries each. From 11:20: alternates between 58 and 212 entries (11:20 212; 11:25 58; 11:30 212; 11:35 212; 11:40 58). The 212-entry files repeat every feature name 3 to 4 times. The generating query ran on analytics-db nodes 1-6 for the 212-entry files and nodes 9-16 for the 58-entry ones.

analytics_db_query.description: Result of the feature-list query on one migrated and one unmigrated analytics-db node.
analytics_db_query.result: Node 3 (grants migrated at 11:12): 'SELECT name, type FROM system.columns WHERE table = bot_features' returns 212 rows: each column listed once for database 'default' and again for each underlying shard database 'r0'-'r2'. Node 12 (not yet migrated): 58 rows, 'default' only.

bot_score_service.description: bot-score service error rate and latency.
bot_score_service.result: v8.4 since 10:40: error rate 0.03%, p99 latency 11ms, unchanged from v8.3. edge-proxy calls to bot-score dropped by 40% during the 5xx bursts because requests fail before the call.

kv_store_health.description: Edge key-value store errors and dependencies.
kv_store_health.result: KV read errors 0.1% until 11:21, then swing with the edge 5xx rate. KV reads are served through the edge-proxy; the KV storage backend reports 0 errors and p99 latency 6ms throughout.

analytics_db_logs.result: QUERY FAILED: log search timed out after 30s. 0 lines returned. This is a failed query, not an empty result.

email_queue.result: Queue depth 1,200 messages, drained within 2 minutes on average. A marketing send started at 11:00 as scheduled.

disk_alerts.result: logs-archive-07 at 86% disk (warning at 85%) since 08:00. No other disk alerts.

office_vpn.result: London office VPN reconnect storm at 11:02-11:04 UTC after a firewall firmware update; stable since.

dns_resolution.description: DNS resolution success and latency for edge and origin names.
dns_resolution.result: Resolution success 99.99%, p99 12ms throughout 10:00-11:40 UTC. The provider's maintenance touched only its management API.

guidance: A failed query (like a timeout or a locked table) means the check itself could not complete. It is not evidence that nothing happened. An empty result from a wrong service name means the query was malformed, not that there is nothing to find. Neither should be cited as evidence in a root cause analysis.
